newsitem.title: USA: Intl cotton group cuts China 96/97 cotton estimate.
newsitem.headline: Intl cotton group cuts China 96/97 cotton estimate.

text.p: The International Cotton Advisory Committee (ICAC) Wednesday said it lowered its forecast for China 1996/97 cotton production to 3.7 million tonnes from 4.1 million tonnes.
ICAC statistician Terry Townsend said the group had reduced its estimate because planted area was "considerably lower" than previously thought.
Townsend said his group is basing its forecast on 4.4 million hectares planted and cautioned that the estimate could be revised again.
"There's a tremendous range of error around the production forecast in China because the country is so big and we know so little about it," Townsend said in an interview.
Townsend predicted lower production this year will not have a big impact on China cotton imports because stocks are huge and there is a lag in buying decision-making.

Townsend noted China will lose its slot as the world's largest cotton producer to the United States if production declines and the U.S. harvest matches the approximately 4.1 million tonnes forecast by the U.S. Agriculture Department.
The China 1995/96 cotton crop stood at 4.8 million tonnes, according to the ICAC.
